verses.english: So It Was Said 97
The Book of the Threes
Chapter Five
Good Morals
This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

verses.pali: “Kalyāṇasīlo, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇadhammo kalyāṇapañño imasmiṁ dhammavinaye ‘kevalī vusitavā uttamapuriso’ti vuccati—
verses.english: “Mendicants, in this teaching and training a mendicant of good morals, good practice, and good wisdom is called consummate, accomplished, a supreme person.
And how does a mendicant have good morals?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati, ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇasīlo hoti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant has good morals.
Such is one of good morality.
And how does one have good practice?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sattannaṁ bodhipakkhiyānaṁ dhammānaṁ bhāvanānuyogamanuyutto viharati.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant meditates pursuing the development of the seven qualities on the side of awakening.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇadhammo hoti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant has good practice.
Such is one of good morality and good practice.
And how does one have good wisdom?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom in this very life. And they live having realized it with their own insight due to the ending of defilements.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇapañño hoti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant has good wisdom;

verses.pali: Iti kalyāṇasīlo kalyāṇadhammo kalyāṇapañño imasmiṁ dhammavinaye ‘kevalī vusitavā uttamapuriso’ti vuccatī”ti.
verses.english: Such is one of good morals, good practice, and good wisdom, who in this teaching and training is called consummate, accomplished, a supreme person.”
The Buddha spoke this matter.
On this it is said:
“Who does nothing wrong
by body, speech or mind,
is said to be one of good morals,
a conscientious mendicant.
Who has well developed the seven
factors that lead to awakening
is said to be one good practice,
an unpretentious mendicant.
Who understands for themselves
the end of suffering in this life
is said to be one good wisdom,
an undefiled mendicant.
One accomplished in these three things,
untroubled, with doubts cut off,
unattached to anything in the world,
has given up everything, they say.”

verses.pali: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
verses.english: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
